ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The remaining part of the chocolate in the figure is an L-shaped right-angled polygon. The top side is labeled 11 cm, the total height on the left side is labeled 6 cm, the vertical side on the right from the top to the notch is labeled 4 cm, and the horizontal side on the left of the bottom is labeled 8 cm. There is a rectangular notch at the lower right corner, indicating the part that has already been eaten. Reasoning: Treat this L shape as a complete circumscribed rectangle minus the small rectangle missing at the lower right. The circumscribed rectangle has width 11 cm and height 6 cm, so its area is 11 × 6 = 66 square centimeters. The width of the missing small rectangle is 11 − 8 = 3 cm, and its height is 6 − 4 = 2 cm, so its area is 3 × 2 = 6 square centimeters. Therefore the remaining area is 66 − 6 = 60 square centimeters. Each piece of chocolate is 1 cm × 1 cm, that is, each piece has area 1 square centimeter, so the number of remaining chocolate pieces is 60.

method.method_draft: Read the image as an L-shaped remaining chocolate tablet: the full outer rectangle would be 11 cm wide and 6 cm tall, with a rectangular corner missing at the lower right. From the labels, the missing corner has width 11−8=3 cm and height 6−4=2 cm. Compute the remaining area as the outer rectangle area minus the missing corner area: 11×6−3×2=66−6=60. Since the text states each square piece is 1 cm by 1 cm, the number of remaining pieces equals the area in square centimeters, so John still has 60 pieces.

推理：把这个 L 形看作一个完整的外接长方形减去右下角缺失的小长方形。外接长方形宽 11 cm、高 6 cm，面积为 11 × 6 = 66 平方厘米。缺失小长方形的宽为 11 − 8 = 3 cm，高为 6 − 4 = 2 cm，面积为 3 × 2 = 6 平方厘米。所以剩余面积为 66 − 6 = 60 平方厘米。每块巧克力是 1 cm × 1 cm，即每块面积 1 平方厘米，因此剩余巧克力块数为 60。
